items.title: [model] fix: unpack visual output in Qwen2-VL and GLM4V dummy forward paths
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

- Fix text-only (and mixed-modality) training failures for **Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL ** when using recent `transformers`, where `model.visual()` returns a structured output (e.g. `BaseModelOutputWithPooling`) instead of a raw tensor.
- Route **dummy** and real visual forwards through `unpack_visual_output` in `qwen2_vl.py` and `glm4v.py`, matching the pattern already used in `qwen3_vl.py`.
- **Keep** the text-only dummy visual forward from [#5881](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/5881) (out-of-place `inputs_embeds + 0.0 * …`) so vision weights stay on the autograd graph and FSDP/DDP usage stays aligned across ranks.


**Problem**
I found the crash when training Qwen2.5-VL using text-only data (https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/462).
In `_get_input_embeds`, when both `pixel_values` and `pixel_values_videos` are `None` (pure text batch), upstream verl still runs:

Reference: [qwen2_vl.py#L388–L394](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/verl/models/transformers/qwen2_vl.py#L388-L394).
```python
image_embeds = model.visual(pixel_values, grid_thw=image_grid_thw) # Error: it returns `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` instead
inputs_embeds = inputs_embeds + 0.0 * image_embeds.mean() 
```
With recent Hugging Face transformers, Qwen2.5-VL or Qwen2-VL's visual tower returns a structured output (e.g. BaseModelOutputWithPooling with pooler_output / related fields) rather than a plain tensor—see [modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py#L491-L494). That path never uses unpack_visual_output, unlike the real image/video branches in the same function, so image_embeds.mean() is invalid (attribute error / wrong type) and text-only training or rollout fails.

items.title: [Feature] TRITON_MLA: support FP8 KV cache (needed for SM12.0 / Blackwell)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

The TRITON_MLA backend raises `NotImplementedError` when FP8 KV cache is requested:

```python
# triton_mla.py, __init__
if is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
    raise NotImplementedError("TritonMLA V1 with FP8 KV cache not yet supported")

# triton_mla.py, forward_mqa
if self.kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8"):
    raise NotImplementedError("FP8 Triton MLA not yet supported")
```

On SM12.0 (Blackwell — RTX 5080/5090, B100/B200), **TRITON_MLA is the only available MLA backend**:
- `FLASHINFER_MLA` requires `qk_nope_head_dim=128`, but models like GLM-4.7-Flash-REAP have `qk_nope_head_dim=192`
- `CUTLASS_MLA` requires SM10.x

This means FP8 KV cache is completely blocked on Blackwell for these models, even though the base class `MLACommonImpl` already handles FP8 cache writes via `concat_and_cache_mla` (with `_k_scale` quantization in the CUDA kernel) and FlashMLA supports FP8 on other architectures.

## Impact

For VRAM-constrained GPUs (e.g. RTX 5080 with 16 GB), FP8 KV cache would **double the usable context length**. Tested with GLM-4.7-Flash-REAP-23B-A3B NVFP4:
- BF16 KV cache: ~4,928 tokens max context
- FP8 KV cache: ~11,728 tokens max context (2.38×)

## Workaround (not suitable for upstream)

I have a working patch that pre-dequantizes FP8 cache and FP8 query to BF16 before calling the existing Triton decode kernel:

```python
# In forward_mqa, before the Triton kernel:
if self.kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8"):
    k_scale = layer._k_scale.float()
    kv_c_and_k_pe_cache = (kv_c_and_k_pe_cache.float() * k_scale).to(torch.bfloat16)

# Query may also be FP8 (from _decode_concat_quant_fp8_op):
if q.dtype.is_floating_point and q.element_size() == 1:
    q_scale = layer._q_scale.float()
    q = (q.float() * q_scale).to(torch.bfloat16)
```

1. **Full cache dequantization on every decode step** — the entire KV cache page is cast FP8 → float32 → BF16, scaling linearly with sequence length

items.title: [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))
2. **Adapter-only sync missing**: frameworks must merge LoRA → send full weights → unmerge. Adapter-only sync (send only LoRA delta, load via vLLM's LoRA serving) would eliminate the merge round-trip ([trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975))
3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO
- [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776): LoRA + MoE inference mismatch investigation
- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes
- Adapter-only sync path available (no full-weight merge required)

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

items.title: [RFC]: KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters
items.bodyExcerpt:
**Status:** Draft · **PRs:** #58207 (group size), #58380 (prefer `BLHNC`, stacked on #58207)

## TL;DR

Speculative drafters on hybrid models add a small KV cache bucket of their own, which breaks vLLM's KV cache grouping heuristic in two ways:

- **Too many groups (Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash):** a one-layer drafter bucket forces **one group per layer**: Qwen3.5-27B goes from 4 to 70 groups (#49730), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 4 to 46. Each group rebuilds attention metadata every step, so DFlash loses much of its speedup; forcing fewer groups today costs KV cache capacity.
- **Full attention padding (MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash):** the 5-layer drafter bucket sets the group size, which doesn't divide the target's 9 full attention layers, so a full attention padding layer is allocated for the whole context (#58175). Kimi-K3 + DSpark has the same problem: its 5-layer drafter bucket pads the 24 MLA (full attention) layers, with 20 groups.

Checked and unaffected (identical grouping with and without these PRs): GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark.

A two-part proposal fixes both:

| part | problem | fix | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · #58207** | small drafter buckets force per-layer KV groups, or full attn padding | pick the group size by worst-case padding **bytes**; `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) | 46 → **17** groups, **+54%** tok/s @c=1, **+36%** @c=32 | 11 → **7** groups, no full attn padding, KV capacity 5.76M → 5.96M |
| **2 · #58380** | `LBHNC` forces padding when drafter bytes/token ≠ target's | prefer `BLHNC` when the backends can run it and it avoids full attn padding or needs fewer groups | **5** groups, no padding, 7.53M tokens (> main's 7.42M); Triton only today | stays `LBHNC` at 7 groups (`BLHNC` would need 12 and has no full attn padding to remove) |

The parts are complementary: part 2 picks the path; part 1 is the fallback path (§5).

- vLLM 0.30.0 (official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` image), Model Runner V2 (the default for this architecture on 0.30) with async scheduling
- 2 nodes × 8× H100 80GB, pipeline parallel 8 × tensor parallel 2 (PP0–3 on node A, PP4–7 on node B)
- Model: GLM-5.2 FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), `--max-num-seqs 8`

With pipeline parallelism across nodes on Model Runner V2 + async scheduling, configuring **any** KV connector makes decode much slower, even when the connector does nothing. items.bodyExcerpt:
Count prompt-injected thinking spans through the first closing marker, including generations truncated before the marker, while preserving disabled-thinking accounting.

## Purpose

Poolside Laguna's chat template can inject the opening `<think>` token into the generation prompt. Generated token IDs then begin inside the reasoning span and contain only `</think>`, or contain no marker at all when generation is truncated.

`PoolsideV1ReasoningParser` currently inherits the default token counter through `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser`, so the Responses API reports `reasoning_tokens=0` even when the parser emitted a reasoning item.

- counts prompt-opened reasoning up to the first `</think>`; and
- counts all generated tokens when generation truncates before `</think>`.

Fixes #49711.

This is not a duplicate of the related open PRs:

- #49743 handles output containing `</think>` without `<think>`, but its current implementation still returns zero when generation truncates before the closing marker.
- #41077 adds DeepSeek V3 forwarding and GLM-specific absent-start handling; it likewise returns zero when no closing marker is generated.

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.

## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.
- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.
- Searched open PRs for `get_max_prefill_buffer_size`, `max_total_seq_len` and the SM90
  sparse backend; nothing else touches these call sites.

## Testing

No unit test covers either path (both need a GLM-5.3 checkpoint and FlashInfer on
Hopper), so this was validated by serving. 2x H200 NVL, TP2, LibertAI NVFP4 weights,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3, CUDA graphs on, CPU offload

## Purpose

`GLM46VVideoBackend` and `GLMGAVideoBackend` currently find each sampled frame
by iterating over every source frame until its timestamp reaches the next
sampling timestamp. This makes frame-index selection O(source frames), even
though both backends retain at most 640 frames. A long, high-FPS video can
therefore spend several milliseconds in a Python loop before sparse decoding

This change computes the first source-frame index at each sampling timestamp

items.title: [Bugfix] Seed hybrid mamba state index with mamba_block_size on prefix-cache hits
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix an out-of-bounds read on prefix-cache hits for hybrid mamba models whose KV config contains a prefix-cacheable attention group with a block size smaller than `mamba_block_size` (e.g. a DFlash2/EAGLE sliding-window drafter group with block 64).

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`. By then `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has reassigned `cache_config.block_size = min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`, so on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA + sparse MLA, mamba block 7168, drafter block 64/1024) the seed is in the wrong units. `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` takes it as `src_col` and `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`): cached prefixes of ≥ 8 mamba blocks fault (`Xid 31`, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync), shorter hits silently restore the wrong recurrent state.

The fix divides by `cache_config.mamba_block_size`, the unit used for mamba blocks everywhere else (`MambaSpec.block_size`, the preprocess kernel, the block-table width; `mamba_attn.py` already derives the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`).

Fixes #55600.

## Test Plan

No unit test is included; the failure needs a hybrid model whose KV groups include a smaller-block prefix-cacheable group. Manual verification on GLM-5.3-Flash (EXL3, TP=1, DFlash2 `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `max_num_seqs=1`) on a DGX Spark, before/after on identical inputs.

## Test Result

- Prompt A = 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question: before → HTTP 500 in 0.2 s, `NVRM: Xid 31 ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`; after → completes in 11.7 s with 50 176 cached tokens.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). items.title: [Perf][Attention] Remove D2H sync from FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The persistent-topk kernel can miss higher-scoring entries, and the entries it misses depend on atomic ordering, so identical runs can differ.

On a GB10, rows of 6000 to 32768 candidates with tight score distributions drop 89 to 6603 winners across five rows.

We can add detection for overflow which add one extra comparison/load on the hot paths for cases that do not overflow. On overflow, we select the bin's top members exactly with a byte-wise radix pass over the row. In the vast majority of cases this is not hit. On the fast path, we are within 1 to 2 µs at 25 to 55 µs per call. The fallback itself, which should be rare outside of the failure case, costs ~2 µs per call at about 10k pools and ~18 µs at about 30k pools.

`radix_topk` has no capped buffer and is unaffected. `FilteredTopKUnifiedKernel`, `cooperative_topk`, and `histogram_4096_topk` have the same buffer limit pattern on sm_90 and sm_100 and are not changed here...  PRs to follow there. (see #53287 as well)

items.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Name the layer when a MoE expert weight is unquantized
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A ModelOpt checkpoint can store a MoE submodule unquantized while leaving it out of the
quantization exclude list. The layer is then built for packed low-precision weights and the
weight loader is handed a floating point tensor of the logical width, so the load dies inside
`Tensor.copy_` with a message that names neither the layer nor the cause:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

The two numbers differ by exactly 2, which is the FP4 packing factor, but it reads like a
tensor-parallel sharding bug. The ratio is identical at every TP size, so the obvious
experiment (change `--tensor-parallel-size`) costs a full model load and proves nothing. The
traceback ends in a generic loader and names no module, so there is nothing to grep for.

This PR raises a targeted error instead. The check only fires where `copy_` would already
fail, so no configuration that loads today changes behaviour.

### The checkpoint that prompted it

`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` has `num_hidden_layers: 45` and `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, so
layer 45 is the MTP layer. Reading the safetensors headers, layer 45 is unquantized and layer
44 is not:

| tensor | layer 44 | layer 45 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight` | `U8 (2048, 2048)` | `BF16 (2048, 4096)` |
| `mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight_scale` | `F8_E4M3 (2048, 256)` | absent |
| whole-layer dtypes | 864 `U8` + 864 `F8_E4M3` | 888 `BF16` + 1 `F32` |

`quantization_config.ignore` has 132 entries covering layers 0 to 44 and nothing matching
layer 45, so `is_layer_excluded()` returns False and the experts are built NVFP4. The
checkpoint's own `.quant_summary.txt` lists layer indices 0 to 44 only, so ModelOpt never
processed the MTP layer. Adding a pattern for that layer to the exclude list makes the config
describe the weights, and the model then serves with MTP at 75% draft acceptance.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #56564.

`_get_backend_priorities` inserts `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` at the **front** of the SM90 sparse list whenever `head_size == 512`:

```python
sparse_tail = [FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE, FLASHMLA_SPARSE]
if head_size == 512:
    sparse_tail.insert(0, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90)
```

GLM-5.3-Flash is NoPE MLA (`kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=0`), so `head_size = 512` and the condition fires. The first four non-sparse candidates are rejected (the model requires sparse), which makes the winner whatever leads `sparse_tail`. Once FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 satisfies `has_flashinfer_sm90_nope_mla()` (the `ckv_scale_arr` kwarg check), the SM90 FlashInfer sparse backend is selected by default.

The reported measurements on H100 (#56564) put that backend **36% behind `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` at concurrency 1 and 70% behind at concurrency 8** (output 754 → 230 tok/s), with **identical MTP acceptance length** — so the gap is the per-step attention kernel, not the drafting path. The issue reporter re-confirmed on nightly `7f1a539` / FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 that the priority is unchanged and the workaround is still an explicit `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`.

## Change

Drop the `head_size == 512` special case: NoPE-512 and DeepSeek-576 now share one SM90 sparse order, with `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` kept last as a fallback for hosts where the FlashAttention sparse path is unavailable. No behavior change for 576, for SM100/SM120, or for the non-sparse lists.

- The `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` TMA-descriptor log spam (#56563) was fixed by #55385.

items.title: [ROCm][Model][Bugfix] Fix GLM-5.2 shared-expert fusion and MTP on the ROCm DSA path
items.bodyExcerpt:
#51915 aliased `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` onto `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/`. That enabled GLM-5.2-MXFP4 there, but it also moved GLM-5.2-FP8 onto a path missing two things the model needs, so the AMD command from the [GLM-5.2 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/zai-org/GLM-5.2) now fails twice on ROCm:

1. **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` can't load the checkpoint** — `KeyError: 'layers.10.mlp.shared_experts.down_proj.weight'`. With fusion on, the checkpoint gives one widened `mlp.shared_experts` tensor per layer. `deepseek_v2.py` splits it into the expert slots appended after the routed experts, but `DeepseekV32Model` subclasses `torch.nn.Module` rather than `DeepseekV2Model`, reimplements `load_weights`, and has no equivalent handling.

2. **MTP kills the engine on the first request** — `AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute 'compact_topk_indices'`. `llm_base_proposer` calls that method once `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is set, which GLM-5.2's config sets. `nvidia/mtp.py` implements it; `amd/mtp.py` never did.

Before #51915, GLM-5.2 fell through to the generic `deepseek_v2` implementation on ROCm, which handles both. This adds the missing pieces rather than changing the routing, so MXFP4 keeps the AMD path.

## Changes

- `amd/model.py`: set `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled`, size the expert params mapping to `n_routed_experts + n_shared_experts`, and split the widened shared-expert tensor into `mlp.experts.{n_routed_experts + j}` — dim 0 for the ColumnParallel gate/up, dim 1 for the RowParallel down. Ported from `deepseek_v2.py` to keep both paths consistent.
- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices`, matching `nvidia/mtp.py`. The ROCm attention already maintains `skip_topk` and `topk_indices_buffer`, so it ports over unchanged.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-module LM heads for multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix two issues with multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2 (MRV2):

1. **Multi-module MTP samples every draft step with module 0's LM head.**
   `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` runs step `i` through MTP module `i` (`spec_step_idx=step`), but `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` calls `self.model.compute_logits(hidden_states)` without `spec_step_idx`. MTP drafters whose `compute_logits` selects the module's own `shared_head` by `spec_step_idx` (Step3.5/3.7, DeepSeek MTP, GLM MTP, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, ...) therefore use module 0's head/norm for all steps. The same applies to the `use_local_argmax_reduction` path (`get_top_tokens`).
   Fix: `sample_draft` goes through two `DraftModelSpeculator` hooks, `compute_draft_logits` and `get_draft_top_tokens`, which ignore the step by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` overrides them to pass `spec_step_idx`, so other drafters (EAGLE, DFlash, ...) are untouched.

2. **Step-3.x MTP cannot run on MRV2** (needed to reproduce 1 end-to-end):
   - The drafter read `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config`, which for the Step-3.7 VLM target is the top-level `Step3p7Config` (`AttributeError: ... 'vocab_size'`), and used the target's quant config (`output_partition_size = 24 is not divisible by block_n = 128`). It is now built from its own text config and draft quant config, as the V1 `Step3p5MTPProposer` does.
   - `load_eagle_model` replaced every MTP layer's `shared_head.head` with the target `lm_head` because `Step3p5MTP` has no top-level `lm_head`. Step-3.7's three MTP heads differ from the target `lm_head` (checked in the checkpoint), so this collapsed position-0 acceptance from 0.93 to 0.06. `Step3p5MTP` now declares `has_own_lm_head = True`, and `_should_share` keeps a declared-own copy that has no top-level module.
